FF-A MAIN_HOLD: D1=1; rising MAIN_REQ sets Q1=FET_RELEASE. /CLR1=MAIN_CLR_N=POR_OK & TMR_TRIG(PRE_USED) & TMR_DONE & PRE_OK & BQ_DDSG_OK & BMS_LOCAL_OK. Timer completion, both comparator outputs, BQ permission and local permit must all be true before the asynchronous clear releases. Loss of any condition asynchronously drops FET_RELEASE; restoration cannot reclose without a fresh MAIN_REQ rising edge. /PRE1=1.
FF-B PRE_USED: D2=1; rising MCU PRE_REQ sets Q2=TMR_TRIG (direct LTC6993-1 TRIG and one-shot-used state). /CLR2=POR_OK, so it rearms only after physical power-off/POR; /PRE2=1. Q2 stays high for the rest of the powered session and cannot retrigger the LTC6993. PRE_REQ and MAIN_REQ have external 100kΩ pulldowns; MCU sequencing is ordinary software state management, while timer, comparator window, BQ permission, local permit, POR and BQ BOTHOFF remain hard gates.
BQ76952 U1 cross-sheet requirement: DDSG physical pin 32 -> BQ_DDSG_OK; Settings:Configuration:DDSG Pin Config 0x9302=0xA2 (PIN_FXN=2 DDSG, OPT5=1 active-low fault, OPT3=1 REG1 drive; 0x9236 REG12 Config requires REG1_EN=1 and REG1V[2:0]=6 (3.3V; if REG2 is disabled the byte is 0x0D)). Datasheet default is 0x00 unused, so keep BQ_DDSG_OK pulled low until configured. Enable Settings:Protection:Enabled Protections C 0x9263 bit1 HWDF=1 (default 0); ensure DSG FET Protections C 0x926B bit1 HWDF=1 (default byte 0xE2 already has bit1 set); configure a finite HWD delay. DFETOFF pin config 0x92FB=0x42 (PIN_FXN=2, OPT4=1 BOTHOFF, OPT5=0 active-high) is required for Q_DFETOFF high to hard-disable CHG/PCHG/DSG/PDSG.
LTC6993-1: rising-edge non-retriggerable one-shot; current 68.1kΩ RSET and DIV network target nominal 2.855s. With ±3% timer accuracy and ±1% RSET, first-order interval is about 2.74–2.97s before divider/rail/threshold effects. FF-B holds TRIG high after one edge, so the trigger is not shortened when PRE_REQ falls. Timer end cuts the QPRE window; MCU may request MAIN_HOLD only after timer completion, PRE_OK, BQ permission and local permit all hold. PRE_USED remains set until physical power-off/POR, preventing another timer run in the same powered session.
